verses.text: “I’m worn out with my life. I’m going to let my complaint out and speak from the bitterness deep inside me.
I’ll tell God, ‘Don’t condemn me. Show me why you’re taking up a case against me.
Does it please you to crush me, look down on what your own hands made, and smile on the plans of the wicked?
Do you have eyes made of flesh? Do you see things the way people do?
Are your days like a mortal’s days, or your years like a person’s years,
that you have to dig for my wrongdoing and search for my sin?
You know I’m not wicked, and there’s nobody who can rescue me from your hand.
“‘Your hands shaped every part of me, and now you’re tearing me down.
Please remember that you shaped me like clay. Are you going to turn me back into dust?
Didn’t you pour me out like milk and let me thicken like cheese?
You wrapped me in skin and flesh and knitted me together with bones and sinews.
You gave me life and showed me faithful love. Your care kept my spirit alive.
Yet you kept these things hidden in your heart. I know this is what you had in mind:
If I sin, you’ll take note of it, and you won’t clear me of what I’ve done.
If I’m wicked, I’m in for trouble. Even if I’m in the right, I still can’t lift my head. I’m full of shame and painfully aware of what I’m suffering.
If I lift my head, you hunt me like a lion. You show me your power all over again.
You bring fresh witnesses against me, and your anger at me keeps growing. Wave after wave of battle comes against me.
“‘So why did you bring me out of the womb? I wish I’d breathed my last before anyone saw me.
It would’ve been as if I’d never existed. I would’ve been carried straight from the womb to the grave.
Haven’t I got just a few days left? Stop and leave me alone so I can find a little comfort,
before I go to the place I’ll never come back from, the land of darkness and the shadow of death,
a land as dark as midnight, where the shadow of death hangs over everything, where nothing is in order and even the light is like midnight.’”
